summary: Registers the URN namespace identifiers bbf, broadband-forum-org and dslforum-org for naming resources published by the Broadband Forum.

eli5.summary: Each group gets its own prefix for naming things so names do not clash. This gives the Broadband Forum its prefixes.

questions: how do organizations register urn identifiers
subtitle: Unique naming identifiers for Broadband Forum specifications and resources

tldr.problem: The Broadband Forum needs unique, persistent identifiers for the specifications and data models it publishes. Without registered namespaces, names could clash with others.
tldr.mechanism: This RFC registers three URN Namespace Identifiers (NIDs) following RFC 3406: 'bbf' for new work, 'broadband-forum-org' and 'dslforum-org' for Customer Premises Equipment (CPE) management protocol data models.
tldr.outcome: Broadband Forum can use stable, globally unique URN identifiers to name resources like data models and XML schemas, enabling persistence and preventing collisions.

facts.label: Primary use
facts.value: Data models, XML schemas, YANG modules

today: RFC 8057 is an Informational RFC that registered the three URN namespaces and remains in effect. Broadband Forum continues to assign identifiers under these namespaces for its specifications and data models. The registration allows BBF's standards (particularly CPE management protocols and data models) to be referenced with stable, globally unique names. This supports long-term interoperability: software written today can reference a resource via its URN and expect the reference to remain valid for decades.

sections.title: Who Is the Broadband Forum and Why Names Matter
sections.content:
The Broadband Forum (BBF) is a non-profit industry alliance that develops broadband networking specifications. Its work covers home networks, access networks, and backbone networks for residential and business broadband services. Major operators and equipment vendors participate. BBF has been publishing specifications for decades, including standards for Customer Premises Equipment (CPE) management protocols.

When an organization publishes many specifications, it needs a way to give each resource (a data model, an XML schema, a protocol identifier) a unique, persistent name that does not change and does not clash with anyone else's names. Uniform Resource Names (URNs) provide this. A URN like urn:bbf:yang:broadband-forum-org:tr-181-2-0-broadband-forum-cwmp uniquely identifies a data model. The first part (the Namespace Identifier or NID) is registered with IANA; the rest (the Namespace Specific String) is managed by the organization.
sections.eli5: BBF writes lots of standards. They need unique names for all of them so they do not get mixed up with other groups' names.

sections.title: The Three Registered Namespaces
sections.content:
BBF (Namespace ID: 'bbf') is the new primary namespace. BBF uses it for all new work efforts related to data models for protocols other than CPE WAN Management Protocol (CWMP). Examples might include data models for broadband access networks, home gateways, or emerging technologies. The namespace structure follows RFC 2141 syntax rules.

broadband-forum-org (Namespace ID: 'broadband-forum-org') covers all data models related to CWMP, the CPE WAN Management Protocol defined in TR-069. CWMP is the standard for remotely managing home routers and other customer equipment. This namespace has been in use for many years by BBF and is now formally registered. It manages thousands of data model definitions.

dslforum-org (Namespace ID: 'dslforum-org') is another CWMP-related namespace. BBF was formerly known as the DSL Forum before its 2008 name change. This namespace preserves backward compatibility with older CWMP-related specifications and data models published under the old name. Legacy implementations and specifications still reference this namespace.
sections.eli5: Three naming prefixes: 'bbf' for new stuff, 'broadband-forum-org' for equipment management, 'dslforum-org' for old names from before the name change.

sections.title: How the Namespaces Work
sections.content:
Each registered namespace follows RFC 3406 registration procedures. BBF is the Designated Registrant and manages all resource names within each namespace. BBF publishes the assigned resources on its Assigned Resources web page [BBF-RESOURCES].

For uniqueness: BBF guarantees that each name string assigned in its namespaces is unique. BBF may designate secondary responsibility for certain resource classes (allowing partners to assign names under BBF supervision). For experimental testing, BBF may allocate temporary experimental values, with the understanding that multiple users might use the same values for testing and names could collide.

For persistence: BBF maintains the BBF Assigned Resources web page listing all registered resources. The URN assigned to a data model remains the same forever, even if the underlying specification is updated or superseded. This persistence is crucial: code that was written five years ago can still reference a URN and find the resource.

Assignment procedures are published on the BBF web site. There is no resolution discovery system (no automatic way to look up a URN online), but the BBF web page serves as the manual registry.
sections.eli5: BBF hands out names one at a time, writes them all down, and promises never to change them or give the same name twice.

sections.title: Examples and Practical Use
sections.content:
A typical URN in the 'bbf' namespace might be: urn:bbf:yang:broadband-forum-org:tr-181-2-0-broadband-forum-cwmp, identifying a specific version of a CWMP data model defined in BBF Technical Report TR-181. The structure conveys what the resource is (a YANG data model), what it covers (CWMP), and its revision level.

For the 'broadband-forum-org' namespace (legacy CWMP resources): urn:broadband-forum-org:cwmp-dt:tr-098-1-4 might identify a data type definition in an older CWMP specification.

For the 'dslforum-org' namespace (pre-name-change): urn:dslforum-org:cwmp:tr-069-1-3 would preserve references to a TR-069 specification published when the organization was still called DSL Forum.

These URNs are used in XML schemas, YANG data models, YANG module names, and protocol specifications to uniquely identify resources. A network management system can reference a URN to know exactly which version of a data model it implements.
sections.eli5: A name might say: 'this is a CWMP model, version 2.0, from the broadband forum, called TR-181.' That exact name never means anything else.

sections.title: Trust and Verification
sections.content: URN registration does not provide strong cryptographic verification. The registration establishes that BBF is the authoritative source for names in its namespaces, but applications using these URNs may want additional verification (such as checking the actual specification document against digital signatures). BBF's continued management of the resource registry and maintenance of the Assigned Resources web page provides practical assurance that names remain stable and consistent. The registration record itself includes contact information for BBF's namespace manager, allowing anyone with questions about a resource to reach the responsible organization. Organizations that build systems around these URNs should verify the authenticity of specifications by checking BBF's official publications, not by trusting URNs alone.
sections.eli5: A name tells you where to look, but check the actual document to make sure it is real.
